answer: Because the entropy is measured at the yarrow gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the ivory audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 119 variations of one paragraph as a result pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the bridge panel. That is 23 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
